kangaroo-at-2013-student-14.prompt: We are looking at the following statement about a function $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ defined for all integers $x$: "For each even $x$, $f(x)$ is even." What would be the negation of this statement?

choices.text: There is an even number $x$ for which $f(x)$ is odd.
There is an odd number $x$ for which $f(x)$ is odd.

kangaroo-at-2013-student-16.reviewNote: Official answer (C) 3 counts the cases where the non-square piece has area 4 (L = 5.8, 1, 4). Read literally ('one of which'), L = 2 (square 2x2 of area 4 plus a 2x3 rectangle) would also qualify, giving 4.

So I asked the smaller one whether the taller one is a Truthteller. He answered and then I knew which type they both were. Which statement is correct?

The taller one was a Liar and the smaller one a Truthteller.
